capabilities.name: domi-consumer
capabilities.description: Use when working in (or unsure whether you're in) a repository that consumes DomI — to detect the .domi-pin, report drift status (current/behind/forked/unverifiable/malformed), and see which inherited policy categories are owned upstream. Reports; never vendors or reimplements DomI-owned policy.

capabilities.name: fork-pr-flow
capabilities.description: Use when opening, targeting, or describing a pull request and deciding where changes land — whether the repo is a fork (origin vs upstream, avoiding "upstream into upstream") or one you own where changes should reach your own main via PR rather than a direct commit; also when unsure whether to push at all, or when tempted to merge a PR you just opened because you have access and were told to "get it merged".

capabilities.name: hands-on-keyboard
capabilities.description: Use when the user wants to stay hands-on while working with Claude instead of fully delegating — pairing/navigator sessions, learning or practicing a workflow, or signals like "walk me through this," "don't just write it for me," "explain before you touch anything," or "I want to type this myself." Also use when Claude notices it is about to make a string of unreviewed edits and the stakes or learning value of pausing are non-trivial.

capabilities.name: license-compliance-auditor
capabilities.description: Use when auditing a repository for license compliance — reconciling the declared license against dependencies, vendored code, submodules, fonts, bundled assets, datasets, and copied snippets; classifying risk and obligation gaps; never giving legal conclusions.

capabilities.name: maintain-claude-md
capabilities.description: Use when a repo needs its CLAUDE.md created, updated, or checked — scaffolding a new CLAUDE.md from repo introspection, appending a dated lesson or new active-spec note after a session, or linting an existing one for broken @-includes, dead loader-stubs, stale references, unexplained hard rules, duplicated governance, or unsafe command snippets. Also when asked to run /maintain-claude-md in any mode.

capabilities.name: repo-hygiene-init
capabilities.description: Use when setting up a new or bare repo, or when asked to add "repo hygiene", tooling, automation, pre-commit, editorconfig, linting/formatting, a Makefile, a LICENSE, a README, or to pick a versioning scheme — bootstrapping the baseline quality scaffolding a project should have.

capabilities.name: scoped-sequential-prs
capabilities.description: Use when splitting a large or messy change into an ordered series of clean, single-purpose PRs — reconstructing history into staged PRs, keeping each PR strictly in scope, or preventing later-phase code and prose from leaking into an earlier PR.

capabilities.name: session-continuity
capabilities.description: Use when starting or ending a working session, writing a handoff prompt for a future session, or deciding where session notes and project profiles should live — including when a session is about to end with undocumented decisions, or notes are about to be written inside a project repo.

capabilities.name: verify-then-commit
capabilities.description: Use when about to commit or push after making or resuming changes — especially after a subagent or another session edited code, before claiming work is done, or when tempted to commit because edits "look right" without running the project's tests, typecheck, and lint.

capabilities.name: handoff
capabilities.description: Generate a clean, scope-bounded prompt for a future session (Claude Code, Fable, or Codex)

capabilities.name: license-audit
capabilities.description: Audit this repo for license compliance (deps, vendored code, fonts, assets, datasets, snippets).

capabilities.name: notes-home
capabilities.description: Show, set, migrate, or reset the Bindle notes home (point it at an Obsidian vault)

capabilities.name: project-profile
capabilities.description: Create or update the portable project profile in the notes home (explicit export only)

capabilities.name: promote-insight
capabilities.description: Classify one insight and route it to its home (skill, project rule, profile, gate, privacy rule) with explicit confirmation

capabilities.name: session-end
capabilities.description: Close out the session — write a durable session note (outside the repo) and surface candidate improvements

capabilities.name: session-start
capabilities.description: Orient a new session — repo state, project profile, prior notes, validation gates

capabilities.name: workflow-review
capabilities.description: Review recent session notes/profiles/handoffs for recurring friction and promotable patterns

capabilities.name: promote-knowledge
capabilities.description: Promote project evidence into the living project map — propose, confirm, write

capabilities.name: knowledge-scout
capabilities.description: Use when /promote-knowledge needs the evidence set digested — reads the given notes-home files (and inline issue/PR extracts) and returns rung-classified promotion candidates per docs/knowledge-promotion.md. Read-only; never writes files; never promotes.

capabilities.name: claude
capabilities.description: Bindle's global preferences and hard rules installed to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for every Claude Code session: branch/PR discipline gated on an observable repo signal, verify-before-commit, and other universally-safe defaults.

capabilities.name: agents
capabilities.description: Bindle's global preferences for Codex, installed to an explicit --codex-home target's AGENTS.md: the Codex-native equivalent of global/CLAUDE.md, including project-context guidance.

capabilities.name: bindle
capabilities.description: Stable public Bindle CLI dispatcher: resolves the installed checkout root, prints version/help, and delegates context/map/evidence/doctor commands to the existing helper authorities without duplicating domain logic.

capabilities.name: session-context
capabilities.description: Emit a compact, budget-capped orientation blob for the current project (notes-home resolution, latest session note/handoff paths, open in-progress issues, a one-line git summary); run on every Claude Code session start via global/hooks/session-start-context.py.

capabilities.name: slugify
capabilities.description: Canonical, dependency-free implementation of the session-continuity slug rule (lowercase, collapse non-[a-z0-9] runs to one '-', trim edges) for notes-home path segments; self-tested via --self-test, wired into bin/check.sh.

capabilities.name: notes-home
capabilities.description: Inspect and durably configure where Bindle's session workflows keep their notes (docs/notes-home.md): status/set/migrate/reset against BINDLE_NOTES_DIR, with a surgical, confirm-before-write settings.json edit; backs the /notes-home command.

capabilities.name: domi-status
capabilities.description: Read-only DomI-consumer detector: parses a repo's .domi-pin and reports a compact drift verdict (current/behind/forked/unverifiable/malformed/not-a-domi-consumer) by delegating the drift check to DomI's own offline_drift_check.sh (an offline sibling-clone comparison), mirroring DomI's check_pin.sh exit-code contract; never reimplements DomI-owned policy.

capabilities.name: session-notes-format
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral session-continuity contract (notes home, naming, artifact shapes, privacy rules) extracted from the session-continuity skill and commands, with explicit contract levels; the session-continuity skill automates it for Claude Code, and Codex follows it directly.

capabilities.name: hands-on-keyboard-contract
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral contract for a navigator/driver collaboration mode: roles, the default interaction loop, escalation modes, decision checkpoints, and how to follow it manually from Codex or another assistant; the hands-on-keyboard skill is the Claude-native automation of this contract.

capabilities.name: delegated-implementation-packets
capabilities.description: The reusable contract for turning an approved issue into a bounded, subagent-ready implementation packet: ten required sections, a copyable template, a worked example, and the plan-only vs. authorized-implementation split.

capabilities.name: delegation-profiles
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral ladder (Mechanical, Review, Research, Implementation, Privileged) for what a delegated worker is authorized to do, independent of which model or provider executes it; a packet names a profile from this contract without naming a model.

capabilities.name: workflow-composition
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral classification and precedence contract (Invariants, Project instructions, Modes, Task workflows, Provider adapters) for what happens when more than one workflow applies to the same task, the narrow-or-add relaxation rule, and how a delegated task inherits each category.

capabilities.name: workflow-eval
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral policy for what kinds of evaluation a workflow needs and how much, scaled to risk: seven eval categories, a risk-based minimum-coverage matrix keyed to runtime-security-privacy.md's C0-C5 classes, a state-based/model-graded result schema, and a rep-count stopping rule grounded in this repo's existing pressure-test practice.

capabilities.name: capability-inventory
capabilities.description: The schema reference (fields, enums) and completeness model (bijection for skill/command/agent/global-guidance; classified not_a_capability ledger for scripts/contracts) for capabilities.json, plus the "how to add a capability" workflow, including the skill-portability-audit.md bound-table coupling; the inventory's own normative contract.

capabilities.name: privacy-boundaries
capabilities.description: What counts as private for this repo, where private content is allowed to live, and the guardrails that keep it out of Git; enforced automatically for Claude via bin/check-private-info.sh and followed directly by Codex per using-bindle-with-codex.md.

capabilities.name: knowledge-promotion
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral knowledge-promotion contract (promotion ladder, project-map format, cursor and evidence semantics, promotion report) from the #81 design; /promote-knowledge automates it for Claude Code, and Codex or a human follows the manual procedure directly.

capabilities.name: pressure-testing-protocol
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral pressure-testing protocol (arm declaration and void reps, the pre-dispatch fixture checklist, environment controls, transcript grading, cadence, and how reps are recorded) from the #212 campaign findings; every skills/*/PRESSURE-TESTS.md is graded against it, and a human or any provider follows it directly.

capabilities.name: domi-consumer
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral contract for detecting and reporting a DomI-consumer dependency: .domi-pin schema, the status vocabulary mirroring DomI check_pin.sh, source-of-truth/ownership rules, write-work gating, and the inherited-policy category→authority map; bin/domi-status.sh is the executable adapter and the domi-consumer skill is the Claude-native automation.

capabilities.name: context-graph-schema
capabilities.description: The shipped v1 context-graph interchange contract reference (typed IDs, node/relationship vocabulary, endpoint matrix, candidate-key canonicalization, validation model) implemented by bin/context_graph/ and schemas/context-graph/v1/ — issue #180, epic #140.

capabilities.name: package-release-integrity
capabilities.description: Use when validating whether a Python package release is safe to cut — checking version-source agreement, tag/version consistency, changelog presence, and correct semver movement (including data-only track routing) before publish. Judgment calls (change classification) must be supplied, never guessed. Defers to DomI where a well-formed .domi-pin makes its release-semver-governance category authoritative; never itself authorizes publishing.

capabilities.name: package-release-integrity
capabilities.description: Provider-neutral contract for validating a Python package release (version-source, tag, changelog, semver movement, tracks) before publish; defers to DomI where a well-formed .domi-pin makes DomI's inherited release-semver-governance category authoritative.

capabilities.name: issue-dedup-scan
capabilities.description: Read-only prior-work dedup scan for a repository issue: deterministically gathers evidence (git history, in-repo specs/plans, open + merged PRs, issue comments) that #<n> may already be worked/done, emitting evidence JSON with the verdict in the exit code (0 no-evidence, 3 evidence-found, 4 uncertain); a failed sub-query yields uncertain, never a clean verdict. Phase-3 adapter for the issue-work-loop contract.

capabilities.name: objective-worktree
capabilities.description: Isolation helper for authorized repository-mutating objective work: fetches origin, resolves origin/main (or a --base ref) to a commit SHA, and creates the objective branch + a dedicated worktree at that exact SHA, emitting the resolved base SHA so a caller cannot merely claim the base was fresh. First stdout line is a verdict token (READY / BLOCKED: origin-unavailable|base-unavailable|branch-exists|worktree-occupied / ERROR) with the exit code carrying the verdict (0/10/1). Phase-4 adapter for the issue-work-loop contract.

capabilities.name: issue-work-loop
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral issue work loop: the six phases (orient, discover, deduplicate, bound+execute, verify, close-out), the state vocabulary, and the two-authority invariant (repository mutation vs external/GitHub mutation are separate grants). Claude automates it via the issue-work-loop skill and bin/issue-dedup-scan.sh; Codex follows it directly.

capabilities.name: release-captain
capabilities.description: The provider-neutral release-decision loop (L1 of #116): six steps (orient, gather evidence, classify, recommend version+timing separately, explain+request authorization, optional Release Please handoff), the none/patch/minor/breaking/uncertain classification and no-release/batch/release-now timing vocabulary, and the invariant that a recommendation is never a release authorization. Recommends and explains only; delegates version-number mapping to repository policy (Bindle's CHANGELOG SemVer rule) and mechanical release-PR/tag/GitHub-Release work to Release Please. The evidence helper (L2), skill (L3), and Release Please wrapper (L4) are deferred.

capabilities.name: release-evidence
capabilities.description: Deterministic release-evidence collector for the release-captain contract (L2 of #116, Step 2): gathers merged PRs + linked issues since the latest tag (commits-since-tag as fallback) and structures them in the contract's evidence-precedence order (release labels → breaking metadata → Conventional-Commit titles → commits → diff as support only), emitting JSON + a human summary. Classifies each change only where a deterministic signal exists and marks everything else uncertain; a label that contradicts the inference is flagged, not overridden; a failed sub-query degrades the verdict to uncertain. Collection layer only — it never decides the final version/timing and never merges, tags, publishes, or releases. Offline dry-run via --fixture (bin/release-evidence-fixtures/).

capabilities.name: map-entry-id
capabilities.description: Stable opaque identity helper for project-map entries (issue #179, epic #140): `allocate --project SLUG` prints one new context-node:<slug>:<32-lowercase-hex> id using command-owned cryptographic entropy (secrets.token_hex(16)) and writes nothing; `validate --map PATH` is read-only structural validation — deterministic discovery of anchored/unanchored entries, marker-placement rules per supported entry shape (decision/learning heading, single-assumption bullet, tension-parent bullet, open-question bullet, typed retirement tombstone), duplicate and malformed identity detection, and bindle:superseded-by validation (missing value, duplicate marker, self-referential, unresolved). Never recomputes an id from mutable entry content; never repairs anything it flags. The two authorized callers are the knowledge-promotion confirmed write (this issue, newly promoted entries only) and #184 anchor acceptance (existing entries) — no other surface allocates a semantic id.

capabilities.name: context-evidence
capabilities.description: Pure, network-free normalizer for typed evidence references (issue #181, epic #140): `normalize` resolves one evidence atom, `normalize-field` tokenizes a complete comma-separated evidence field (respecting Markdown-link and backtick spans as non-separator regions) and normalizes each atom, `normalize-batch` runs a JSONL file of atoms in order. Recognizes typed and bare GitHub issue/PR references (local, repository-qualified, canonical URL), session/handoff/repository-document paths (with traversal/absolute/query rejection and stable repository-binding-qualified identity), commit pointers (recognized but deliberately unresolved), and a narrow whole-value Markdown link wrapper around any of the above — a bare value and its Markdown-linked equivalent always converge on the same canonical id via context_graph.ids. Ambiguous input (a bare GitHub number without a kind hint, a repository-document reference with more than one configured binding) is reported unresolved rather than guessed. Performs no network access and writes nothing.

capabilities.name: context-graph
capabilities.description: CLI entry point for Bindle's context graph (issues #191/#183/#184, epic #140), thin per the #180 adapter pattern — argument parsing and JSON/text rendering only, dispatching into context_graph.config / context_graph.lock / context_graph.compiler / context_graph.review for all domain logic. `init --notes-home DIR --project SLUG [--display-name NAME]` allocates a project identity and creates config.json under the project's .bindle/context directory, reporting `{"created": bool, "config": {...}}` (idempotent: a second call against an existing valid config reports created=false rather than erroring). `config status --notes-home DIR --project SLUG` is read-only: reports the current config plus lock file state (`lock`, `lock_owner_live` — the latter only resolved when the lock's recorded hostname matches the local host). `config validate --notes-home DIR --project SLUG` is read-only structural + semantic validation of the persisted config via context_graph.config.all_findings, printing `{"findings": [...]}` and exiting 1 if any finding is present, 0 otherwise. `config add-repository --notes-home DIR --project SLUG --alias ALIAS --provider PROVIDER [--coordinates COORD] [--local-checkout-path PATH] [--default]` appends one repository binding, allocating its binding_id and reporting `{"repository": {...}, "config": {...}}`. `config update-repository --notes-home DIR --project SLUG --binding-id ID [--alias ALIAS] [--coordinates COORD] [--local-checkout-path PATH] [--default | --no-default]` patches only the supplied fields on one existing binding (the mutually exclusive `--default`/`--no-default` pair set or unset default status; omitting both leaves it unchanged), reporting the same shape. `config remove-repository --notes-home DIR --project SLUG --binding-id ID` deletes one binding, reporting `{"removed": {...}, "config": {...}}`. `config set-default --notes-home DIR --project SLUG --binding-id ID` makes one existing binding the unique default, reporting `{"repository": {...}, "config": {...}}`. `config break-lock --notes-home DIR --project SLUG --force` removes an existing lock file directly (requires --force confirmation), reporting `{"removed_owner": null_or_dict}` and exiting 0 on success, or 1 if --force is absent. `preview --notes-home DIR --project SLUG [--repo-root ALIAS=PATH ...]` (#183) is the read-only, write-nothing deterministic compiler: loads configuration, parses the project map, normalizes evidence through context_graph.evidence, resolves GitHub issues/PRs read-only, constructs deterministic `contains`/`supported_by`/`closes`/`supersedes` nodes and edges (endpoint-validated before admission), emits deterministic identity-anchor candidates for unanchored map entries, and reports conflicts/coverage — printing `{"nodes", "edges", "identity_anchor_candidates", "conflicts", "coverage", ...}` and exiting 0 even when conflicts are present (conflicts are reported, not run failures) or 1 only when configuration is missing/malformed (`context_graph.compiler.CompilerError`). #184 adds three judgment-ledger verbs delegating to `context_graph.review`: `candidates --notes-home DIR --project SLUG [--subject-type edge|identity_anchor] [--status pending|accepted|rejected|retired]` is read-only — the union of live #183 anchor-candidate regeneration and reduced `judgments.jsonl` history, printing `{"rows": [...], "findings": []}` and exiting 0 on success, or 1 when the current graph fails to compile (`context_graph.review.ReviewError`). `propose --notes-home DIR --project SLUG --input PROPOSAL.JSON` loads a proposal envelope via `context_graph.atomic_io.read_json` and validates it against a FRESH #183 preview (writes nothing, takes no lock), printing `{"candidate": dict_or_null, "subject_key": ..., "findings": [...]}` and exiting 0 only when a candidate was produced, 1 otherwise. `confirm --notes-home DIR --project SLUG --candidate-key KEY --decision accepted|rejected|retired [--input PROPOSAL.JSON]` revalidates the named candidate against the CURRENT graph and appends exactly one judgment event under the single-writer "confirm" lock (edge `accepted`/`rejected` requires `--input`; `retired` and all `identity_anchor` decisions do not), printing `{"event": dict_or_null, "idempotent": bool, "findings": [...]}` and exiting 0 only when `findings` is empty. All twelve subcommands accept `--format json|text`; every mutating subcommand except `config break-lock` (`init`, all four `config *-repository`/`set-default` verbs) wraps its domain call in `config.ConfigError` (renders `e.findings`, exit 1) and `lock.LockContention` (renders an `E_LOCK_CONTENTION` finding, exit 1) handling — a not-found binding-id surfaces as a clean findings list, never a traceback. `candidates`/`propose`/`confirm` instead catch `context_graph.review.ReviewError` (raised only when the current graph itself cannot be compiled) and render `exc.findings` the same way, exit 1; `context_graph.atomic_io.read_json` failures on `--input` (`OSError`/`ValueError`) render an `E_INPUT_UNREADABLE` finding and exit 1 rather than a traceback. #185 adds `apply --notes-home DIR --project SLUG [--repo-root ALIAS=PATH ...] [--adopt-context-md]`, which recomputes a fresh #183 preview, reduces #184's judgment ledger against it, and atomically writes `map.md`/`index.json`/`context.md` under the single-writer "apply" lock -- a second apply against an unchanged graph performs zero writes (idempotent), and a per-file write conflict (e.g. an unmanaged or malformed `context.md`) is reported without blocking the other two files' writes; `--adopt-context-md` opts into adopting a still-markerless `context.md`, refusing if it gained markers concurrently. Exits 0 only when `ok` is true and `conflicts` is empty.

capabilities.name: release-captain
capabilities.description: Use for ANY request to release, cut a release, "do a release", decide whether/what/when to release, or "take care of the release" for accumulated work — this is THE release-decision skill and it owns that decision. Gathers evidence since the latest tag, recommends a version class and timing with rationale and confidence, then (only on explicit per-step human approval) drives the configured release strategy to create or update a Release Please release PR. It NEVER cuts the release itself — never bumps VERSION, edits CHANGELOG, commits, tags, publishes, or deploys; those are human-authorized publication. It invokes package-release-integrity as its safety check, and is not replaced by it. Use even when the request sounds like "just handle it".

capabilities.name: release-strategy
capabilities.description: Provider-neutral release-strategy seam for the release-captain workflow (L4 of #116). Reads the single `strategy` key from release-captain.toml and dispatches a verb (which|dry-run|apply) to bin/release-strategies/<strategy>.sh, failing closed (exit 64) on a missing file, missing key, or unknown strategy. Selection only — it performs no release action itself and knows nothing about approval; the orchestrator owns approval and the ephemeral token. No fallback, registry, or discovery.

capabilities.name: local-release-please
capabilities.description: Local Release Please ARTIFACT strategy for the release-captain seam (L4 of #116). Release Please is the artifact authority (VERSION + CHANGELOG + release-PR contents); this strategy assembles `release-please release-pr`: dry-run previews read-only (proves zero mutation), apply creates/updates the release PR and requires an ephemeral --approval-token passed by the orchestrator (no token => hard stop, no invocation). It never merges, tags, creates a GitHub Release, publishes, or deploys — publication stays an explicitly human-authorized action. release-please binary resolved via RELEASE_PLEASE_CMD for test stubbing.

capabilities.name: release-please-sync
capabilities.description: Syncs Bindle's bare VERSION file onto the open Release Please release-PR branch (issue #137): Release Please's extra-files mechanism cannot update Bindle's bare, unannotated VERSION file, so this closes that gap by reading the version Release Please already computed from the PR branch's .release-please-manifest.json and writing it into VERSION, in one follow-up commit pushed onto the same PR branch. dry-run previews read-only; apply requires an ephemeral --approval-token (no token => hard stop). Never creates a new PR, never touches main, never tags, merges, or publishes.

capabilities.name: release-publish
capabilities.description: Manual GitHub Release publish + autorelease relabel (issue #152, problem 1). While GitHub Actions stays billing-blocked, release.yml never fires on a pushed v* tag, so publishing is done by hand; this wrapper replicates release.yml's `gh release create` step exactly (same CHANGELOG-section extraction) and then closes the gap a manual publish otherwise leaves: it ensures the `autorelease: tagged` label exists and moves the just-published merged release PR off `autorelease: pending`, so the next `release-please release-pr` does not abort on an outstanding untagged PR. dry-run previews read-only; apply requires an ephemeral --approval-token (no token => hard stop). Never merges, tags, or opens a PR.

capabilities.name: issue-work-loop
capabilities.description: Use when picking up a repository issue and taking it from discovery to an honest end state — orienting to repo policy, deduplicating before claiming it, bounding and executing the fix, verifying real gates, and closing out with honest status. Automates the six-phase issue-work-loop contract for Claude by delegating each phase to Bindle-native skills; never lets implementation authority imply close/merge/publish authority.

capabilities.name: context-graph
capabilities.description: Use when reviewing, drafting, or confirming semantic relationships in a Bindle context graph, or when the user runs `/context-graph <verb>` — an optional authoring layer over the deterministic context-graph CLI (init / preview / candidates / propose / confirm / apply). It drafts proposals and drives the CLI; it is never the authority for endpoint legality, candidate keys, identities, or acceptance. Not for building the graph's deterministic tooling itself (that is the CLI, issues #180/#183/#184/#185).

capabilities.name: context-graph
capabilities.description: Author and review context-graph semantic proposals over the deterministic CLI (init / preview / candidates / propose / confirm / apply)
